title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 9
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: An investment grows by 8% a year, compounded annually, and is worth £11,664.00 after 2 years. How much was invested?
questions.explanation: Dividing back: £11,664.00 / 1.08² = £10,000.00. Taking 8% off twice instead of dividing gives £9,872.41, because a fall of 8% does not undo a rise of 8%.

questions.prompt: A mix of 64 kg is 5 parts sand to 3 parts cement. How much cement must be added to make the ratio 5 : 4, with no sand added?
questions.explanation: The mix holds 40 kg of sand and 24 kg of cement. Sand is unchanged, so 5 parts is still 40 kg and one part is 8 kg. Four parts of cement is 32 kg, which needs 8 kg more.

questions.prompt: Of 120 students, 78 study French and 54 study German. 9 study neither. How many study both?
questions.explanation: 111 students study at least one language. Adding 78 and 54 gives 132, counting the overlap twice, so the overlap is 132 − 111 = 21. Ignoring the 9 who study neither gives 12.

questions.prompt: Five numbers have a mean of 34. Four of them are 28, 41, 30, 26. What is the fifth?
questions.explanation: Five numbers averaging 34 total 170. The four given total 125, so the fifth is 45. The four alone average 31.25, which is not what the question asks for.

questions.prompt: A circular path 2 m wide runs all the way round a pond of radius 9 m. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation: The path is the area inside radius 11 less the area inside radius 9: (11² − 9²)π = (121 − 81)π = 40π square metres. Squaring the width alone gives 4π, far too small.

questions.prompt: The sum of 5 consecutive integers is 285. What is the largest of them?
questions.explanation: With an odd count the middle integer is the mean: 285 / 5 = 57. The five run 55 to 59, so the largest is 59. 57 is the middle one, not the largest.

questions.prompt: A tank fills in 6 hours through an inlet and empties in 10 hours through an outlet. If both are open, how long does it take to fill from empty?
questions.explanation: The inlet adds 1/6 of the tank an hour and the outlet removes 1/10, a net 1/15, so filling takes 15 hours. Adding the two rates instead of subtracting gives 3.75 hours, which would mean the leak helped.

questions.prompt: A coat is reduced by 30%, and then a further 20% is taken off the reduced price. What single discount has the same effect?
questions.explanation: The price kept is 0.70 × 0.80 = 56% of the original, so the discount is 44%. Adding the two percentages gives 50%, which double-counts the second reduction against the full price.

questions.prompt: A machine has a 5% chance of failing on any given day, independently of other days. What is the probability it fails at least once in 3 days?
questions.explanation: It is easier to find the chance of no failure: 0.95 × 0.95 × 0.95 = 0.8574, so at least one failure has probability 1 − 0.8574 = 14.26%. Multiplying 5% by 3 gives 15%, which counts overlapping outcomes twice.

questions.prompt: A cyclist sets off at 20 km/h. 2 hours later a car sets off along the same road at 60 km/h. How far from the start does the car catch the cyclist?
questions.explanation: The cyclist is 40 km ahead when the car starts, and the car closes at 40 km/h, taking 1 hour. In that hour the car covers 60 km. The 40 km head start is where the cyclist was, not where they meet.

questions.prompt: A van uses 9.5 litres of diesel per 100 km. Diesel costs £1.48 a litre. What does a 260 km journey cost in fuel?
questions.explanation: The journey uses 9.5 × 2.6 = 24.7 litres, costing 24.7 × £1.48 = £36.56. £14.06 is the cost of the first 100 km only.

questions.prompt: If 2 to the power x equals 8 and 3 to the power y equals 81, what is x + y?
questions.explanation: 2³ = 8, so x = 3. 3⁴ = 81, so y = 4. Their sum is 7. Multiplying the two powers together, or adding 8 and 81 in some form, is the usual slip: the question asks for the exponents.

questions.prompt: In an arithmetic sequence the 4th term is 19 and the 9th is 44. What is the first term?
questions.explanation: Five steps separate the 4th and 9th terms, so the common difference is (44 − 19) / 5 = 5. Going back three steps from the 4th term: 19 − 3 × 5 = 4. 5 is the step, not the starting value.

questions.prompt: A bureau offers 1.16 euros to the pound and charges 2.5% commission on the sterling handed over. How many euros does £800.00 buy?
questions.explanation: Commission takes £20.00, leaving £780.00 to convert: £780.00 × 1.16 = 904.80 euros. Converting the full £800.00 gives 928.00 euros and ignores the charge.

questions.prompt: On a map drawn to a scale of 1 : 25,000, two towns are 17.4 cm apart. How far apart are they on the ground?
questions.explanation: 17.4 cm on the map is 17.4 × 25,000 = 435,000 cm on the ground. There are 100,000 cm in a kilometre, so that is 4.35 km. Dividing by 10,000 instead gives 43.5 km.

questions.prompt: 12 kg of tea costing £7.20 a kg is blended with 8 kg costing £11.45 a kg. What does the blend cost per kg?
questions.explanation: The two lots cost £86.40 and £91.60, together £178.00 for 20 kg: £8.90 a kg. Averaging the two prices gives £9.32 and ignores that more of the cheaper tea went in.

questions.prompt: How many integers from 1 to 200 are divisible by 6 but not by 9?
questions.explanation: 33 integers up to 200 are divisible by 6. A number divisible by both 6 and 9 is divisible by 18, and there are 11 of those. Removing them leaves 22. 33 counts every multiple of 6, including the ones to be excluded.

questions.prompt: A ladder 13 m long leans against a wall with its foot 5 m from the base. The foot is pulled out to 12 m from the base. How far does the top of the ladder drop?
questions.explanation: At first the ladder reaches √(13² − 5²) = 12 m. After the foot moves out it reaches √(13² − 12²) = 5 m. The top falls 12 − 5 = 7 m — more than the foot moved out, which is why the two are not equal.

questions.prompt: How many integers n satisfy both 3n − 4 < 20 and n > −2?
questions.explanation: 3n − 4 < 20 gives 3n < 24 and n < 8, so the largest integer is 7. n > −2 makes the smallest -1. From -1 to 7 inclusive there are 7 − (-1) + 1 = 9 integers. Forgetting to count both endpoints gives 8.

questions.prompt: A machine costing £24,000.00 loses 15% of its value each year. What is it worth after 3 years?
questions.explanation: Each year the machine keeps 85% of its value: £24,000.00 × 0.85³ = £14,739.00. Taking 15% of the original price away three times gives £13,200.00, which is lower because it charges the full £3,600.00 every year.

questions.prompt: Both sides of a rectangle are increased by 30%. By what percentage does its area increase?
questions.explanation: Each side is multiplied by 1.3, so the area is multiplied by 1.3 × 1.3 = 1.69 — an increase of 69%. Doubling the 30% gives 60%, which would be right only if one side were fixed.
